newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.8 pct in selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.8 pct in selective trade.

text.p: 1040 GMT - Istanbul shares rose slightly in continued selective activity in utilities on Friday morning, but the market grew cautious as volume fell sharply after the recent strong gains, brokers said.

* The IMKB-100 closed at 95,209.57, up 758.40 points from Thursday's all-time high of 94,451.17 and compared to Thursday's midday record of 95,611.04. Morning volume plunged to 8.22 trillion lira from 16.95 trillion on Thursday.
"The market was in general quiet. The index managed to close at 95,000 levels, but selling may emerge in utilities in the afternoon," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti investment bank.
"If money is not diverted to other stocks, the index may close down at the end of the day," he added.

The index had soared 8.37 percent in the last three days, mainly on utilities and state-owned stocks after Monday's 2.44 percent fall prompted by the S&P's downgrading of Turkey's long-term foreign currency debt rating.
* Of the 231 shares traded, 106 rose, 52 fell and 73 were steady. The 85-share industrial index gained 1.24 percent to 101,601.32 and the 15-share financial index eased 0.17 percent to 90,107.34.
Leading actives were Cukurova Elektrik, up 7,500 lira at 122,500 and Aktas Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 97,000.
